title: Novatech Systems - Private VPC Discovery
summary: Discovery call focused on NovaTech's requirements for a Private/VPC deployment of Redwood. Main concerns: cross-account VPC peering, CIDR overlap, region restrictions (EU-only for some workloads), private control plane, key management, audit logs, and latency for inference. AE + SE covered architecture options (Private deployed control plane vs dedicated hosting), peering patterns, and next steps toward a technical deep dive and security docs exchange.
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC2 + security pack and architecture notes (Ava)
SE to draft VPC peering runbook and sample route tables (Eli)
Customer to provide current VPC CIDR ranges and region restriction list (Priya)
Schedule technical deep dive for latency/benchmarking in the EU region (Eli + Marcus)
action_items: Ava Martinez: Send SOC2 certificate, security questionnaire, and pricing ballpark by 2026-03-22
Eli Chen: Prepare VPC peering runbook, recommended NAT/egress config, and sample cloudformation snippets by 2026-03-23
Priya Desai: Share VPC CIDRs, current peering/topology, and EU-only workload list by 2026-03-22
Marcus Lee: Confirm SIEM log endpoint and retention needs by 2026-03-24
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-20
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Eli Chen (Redwood SE), Jared Kim (CTO - NovaTech), Priya Desai (Cloud Architect), Marcus Lee (Security)

[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick intro, I'm Ava, I'm the AE on the account, with me is Eli our SE. 
[00:10] Jared: Hey Ava, thanks; Jared here. We've been evaluating Redwood for a few weeks. Main thing for us is private deployment - we need VPC-only access, no public internet endpoints for inference.
[00:24] Eli: Got it. Just to confirm, when you say VPC-only do you mean private control plane too, or public control plane with private endpoints?
[00:32] Priya: We'd prefer private control plane. Some of our EU workloads are regulated and have to stay within EU regions and not touch public endpoints. So private control plane + private endpoints would be ideal.
[00:45] Eli: Understood. We support a few deployment modes: Hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and our Private offering which can be VPC-attached with a private control plane. Sometimes people mix the terms - you'll also hear 'Redwood Dedicate' in notes, that's just a transcription quirk. 
[00:59] Marcus: Important: we use an internal SIEM and forward audit logs; must be able to ship audit logs and request logs out to our on-prem or to a specific log endpoint. Also, KMS integration is required, HSM optional.
[01:14] Ava: Yep. Security integrations like KMS and customer-managed keys are supported; we can map out the KMS flow. For logs we typically support pushing to customer endpoints or S3 buckets over private links.
[01:26] Jared: Network-wise, we have a hub-and-spoke with transit gateway. Prefer peering into our spoke VPCs. Can Redwood sit in our account or do we have to host in Redwood's account?
[01:38] Eli: For Private deployments we can do a customer-managed deployment inside your account or a customer VPC peering model. There are pros/cons: in-account gives you more control over routing and security, in-RW-account can simplify upgrades but demands careful IAM.
[01:50] Priya: If you deploy in our account, we need clear IaC examples (terraform/cloudformation) and least privilege IAM roles.
[01:58] Eli: Absolutely, we have sample TF modules. We'll share runbooks.
[02:04] Jared: What about CIDR overlap? We've seen peering get blocked because some vendor VPCs use default 10.0.0.0/8 ranges.
[02:12] Eli: Yes, CIDR overlap is a common blocker. Typical patterns: 1) Ask customer to expand or reassign CIDRs where possible, 2) Use Transit Gateway with NAT/prefix translation (if cloud supports it) or 3) Use PrivateLink-style endpoints instead of peering. We can recommend PrivateLink for overlapping ranges; it depends on bandwidth and latency needs.
[02:34] Priya: Latency for batch inference is fine but we have some low-latency realtime features. How does Dedicated vs Private impact latency?
[02:43] Ava: Dedicated reserved pools are within Redwood's managed infra but isolated for you; latency is usually lower vs shared hosted API because you get reserved GPUs and closer routing. Private in-region inside customer VPC can be best for minimizing egress hops but depends on where model workers run.
[02:58] Eli: A note on regions: you mentioned EU-only. We can pin nodes to eu-west-1 or eu-central-1 but capacity varies. We should validate availability of the model variants you need in the target region; some quantized kernels or GPU types might not be available in every region.
[03:16] Marcus: That availability question is big. We have SLAs per-region. If a model variant isn't available in eu-west-1, can't we fall back to another region?
[03:24] Eli: We can define fallback policies but that would cause data to cross boundaries, which might violate residency. So you'd want strict policies with no fallback for regulated workloads.
[03:34] Jared: How do private endpoints get DNS resolved? We use private hosted zones internally.
[03:40] Eli: We integrate with private DNS or we can provide route53 private hosted zone delegation patterns. There are a couple of options: you host the private zone and create records pointing to the ENIs, or we can publish records into a customer zone with limited permissions. We'll include patterns in the runbook.
[03:56] Priya: Egress — can Redwood avoid NAT Gateway costs? We have significant outbound egress from our VPCs.
[04:04] Ava: If traffic stays within the VPC (private endpoints/ENIs) there shouldn't be NAT egress for inference calls. But if you rely on a public control plane for model management, there might be outbound calls. For fully private control plane running in your account, NAT isn't required.
[04:20] Marcus: For logs we need TLS mutual auth to our SIEM collector, and retention to 7 years for certain logs. Also, audit log integrity — can we get signed logs?
[04:29] Eli: We support pushing logs over private links with TLS; for signed logs we have options to include event digests and can integrate with KMS-backed signing. I'll follow up on exact capabilities.
[04:40] Jared: What about egress to model registries or image pulls — if running in our account does Redwood need to pull images from your registry?
[04:48] Eli: In the in-account model we can run worker nodes under your ECR or use customer-provided images. If using our managed images, we can mirror into your registry or use private registry access with VPC endpoints.
[05:00] Priya: Do you support cross-cloud? We have GCP for some services and Azure for others. Ideally we'd keep inference in AWS EU region.
[05:08] Ava: We support deployments on AWS primarily for Private today; we have options for Azure/GCP in some cases but there are more constraints. If you're AWS-first for EU, that's the simplest.
[05:18] Jared: Ok. Backups and data at rest: encryption at rest with our KMS?
[05:23] Eli: Yes, we can use customer-managed KMS keys for encrypting model artifacts, caches, and logs. Key access can be restricted to specific roles.
[05:31] Marcus: On compliance we need SOC2, ISO27001 docs and an option for dedicated pen-tests.
[05:36] Ava: We'll share SOC2 reports and can coordinate a pen test timeline. We also have an option for annual security reviews for enterprise customers.
[05:45] Priya: Networking specifics — we use /16 and /20 ranges across spokes. We can share exact CIDRs after this call. Also we use a transit gateway with route table isolation per spoke. We don't want vendor VPCs attached to the transit gateway directly, prefer peering into spokes.
[05:59] Eli: That pattern works. We'll propose either peering into the spoke VPCs or using interface endpoints in the spoke and NAT at the spoke if needed. We'll detail both.
[06:10] Jared: Do you support service endpoints like interface VPC endpoints or do you require classic VPC peering?
[06:17] Eli: We can support interface endpoints where supported (PrivateLink) — it's a common solution for overlapping CIDRs. It does add some per-GB costs and may affect throughput; we'll quantify that in the runbook.
[06:30] Marcus: Also want RBAC tied to our SSO — SAML/OIDC. Developer access should be constrained.
[06:36] Ava: We support SSO via SAML and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC can be scoped per-team and per-route. We'll include an access control example.
[06:45] Priya: Any required ports/security groups? Our security team will want a list to pre-approve.
[06:50] Eli: We'll provide a minimal egress/ingress list. Typical: 443 outbound for control plane APIs, plus internal ports for worker-to-worker comms; exact ports depend on whether you host in-account or we host. We'll add those to the runbook.
[07:05] Jared: What's the onboarding timeline for Private in-account? From contract to first requests?
[07:12] Ava: Typically 4-8 weeks depending on network approvals and capacity scheduling. If you go with dedicated reserved capacity it can be 2-4 weeks once contracts are signed.
[07:22] Priya: Can you explain burst capacity? If we have spikes in traffic, how does Redwood handle it for Private?
[07:29] Eli: For Dedicated we offer burst to shared capacity up to a configurable percentage. For Private in-account, burst depends on whether you allow workers to scale out to additional subnets/accounts; we'll need to model that.
[07:40] Jared: Cost model — we'd need a ballpark comparing hosted, dedicated, and private.
[07:45] Ava: We'll send a pricing ranges doc. Quick summary: hosted is pay-as-you-go higher unit price; dedicated is reserved lower unit price with commit; private in-account has ops overhead but can be lowest unit cost at scale. We'll include examples based on your expected RPS.
[07:58] Marcus: For the audit trail, can we get token-level tracing for every inference request? We want to link requests back to user IDs and store that metadata in logs.
[08:08] Eli: Yes, we can surface token-level metadata and request traces; we'll discuss retention and redaction policies with Marcus offline.
[08:17] Priya: Are there any known gotchas with cross-account IAM permissions? For example, the way ENIs are created or if vendor code needs STS assume-role permissions?
[08:26] Eli: We'll outline least-privilege roles. Typically we need an assume-role for deployment and some managed policies. If you want agentless, we can do only private endpoints but that increases network config complexity.
[08:38] Ava: Quick pause — any blockers you already know of?
[08:42] Priya: CIDR overlap is the main one; also procurement wants to ensure log retention costs are predictable.
[08:49] Jared: Timeline is Q2 pilot, production in Q3 if things go well. We need security docs and a network runbook by next week to present to procurement.
[08:59] Ava: We'll prioritize the SOC2 and network runbook. Eli will send the runbook.
[09:04] Eli: I'll include sample route tables, security group policy, PrivateLink options, and Terraform snippets.
[09:10] Marcus: Also include an option for mirrored ECR images and the steps to synchronize images into our account.
[09:16] Eli: Noted.
[09:18] Jared: If we wanted to start with a small pilot, what's the minimum we need?
[09:23] Ava: For a pilot we typically provision a small dedicated pool or in-account private deploy for a single model and a small number of workers. Expect 2-4 weeks provisioning including approvals.
[09:33] Priya: On the topic of model weights — do you host customer model artifacts? We plan to host them in our S3 under strict encryption.
[09:40] Eli: You can host model artifacts in your S3 and we can read them using cross-account access or run workers with permissions to your account. Alternatively we can store it in a customer-encrypted bucket.
[09:51] Jared: Any questions from your side for us?
[09:55] Eli: Yes, can you share the list of models you intend to run and approximate QPS for each?
[10:01] Priya: We'll share a short inventory and QPS estimates — mostly small LLMs for semantic search plus one medium model for chat.
[10:08] Ava: Great. We'll follow up with the security pack and runbook. Any final concerns?
[10:15] Marcus: Make sure the runbook covers the EU-only enforcement and no cross-region fallback.
[10:20] Eli: Will do, we'll include strict routing policies and config examples.
[10:25] Ava: Thanks everyone. Next steps recap: we'll send SOC2 + security pack, Eli will send the VPC peering runbook, and we schedule the technical deep dive next week.
[10:36] Jared: Sounds good. Thanks all.

End of transcript. Note: transcription contains occasional misattributions and small typos (e.g., "Redwood Dedicate" in automated notes).
